plate_findings.evidence: irregular hyperintensive lesions in pallidum, internal capsules, cerebral pedunculis, and right cerebellum hemisphere

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (a, b, c, d). a: T2 MRI of the brain showing hyperintense lesions consistent with Listerial rhombencephalitis, specifically noted in the cerebral peduncles. b: T2 MRI of the brain showing multiple irregular hyperintense lesions, which are consistent with the reported pathology of Listerial rhombencephalitis affecting the described brainstem and cerebellar regions. c: FLAIR MRI slice showing hyperintense lesions, consistent with the context of Listerial rhombencephalitis, although the specific finding is described generally. d: FLAIR MRI slice showing hyperintense lesions, consistent with the context of Listerial rhombencephalitis.

panels.figure_caption: Brain MRI in T2 (a, b) and FLAIR (c, d).
in_text_mentions: In MRI of the brain, in T2 images, nonspecific inflammatory lesions were observed (irregular hyperintensive lesions in pallidum, internal capsules, cerebral pedunculi, and right cerebellum hemisphere) (Figure 1). Because of increasing dyspnoea (SpO2, 73%) and general severe condition of the patient, she was transferred to ICU.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: The panel is an MRI of a human patient showing inflammation and enhancement around the brainstem, consistent with the known presentation of Listeria rhombencephalitis mentioned in the caption and in-text. B: The panel is an MRI of a human patient showing pathology localized to the lower brainstem/cerebellum, which aligns with the diagnosis of Listeria rhombencephalitis.
